guidance.evidence_criterion: Apply a strict action-and-polarity test to the Receiving Party's creation of a new copy or reproduction. An express authorization to make copies supports the hypothesis, subject to its conditions; an operative prohibition or consent-qualified ban opposes it. Do not infer permission from the mere existence, return, destruction, retention, ownership, marking, logging, or certification of copies, from reducing oral information to writing, or from references to counterparts. Cite every independently operative clause that determines whether the Receiving Party may create a copy, together with any necessary subject or list preamble. If the document only mentions existing copies or does not govern creation, treat the hypothesis as unresolved.

Inspect the complete definition and every alternative route by which information becomes Confidential Information. Support the universal identification hypothesis only when identification, marking, or the specified oral-confirmation procedure is required for all covered information. A reasonable-person, inherent-confidentiality, circumstance-based, regardless-of-designation, or other unmarked route opposes it. A marking rule applicable only to one category does not establish the universal statement. Cite the governing definition, all identification conditions, and any operative alternative that defeats universality; otherwise treat the issue as unresolved.

Identify the obligated actor, the material to be returned or destroyed, and the triggering event. Support the hypothesis when the Receiving Party must return or destroy at least some Confidential Information upon termination, expiration, or the stated end of the relationship or purpose. A duty triggered only by a discretionary request does not by itself establish a termination-triggered duty. Do not infer the duty from ownership, certification, permitted destruction, or a clause governing copies alone. Cite the trigger, mandatory action, object, and any exception limiting what must be returned or destroyed.

Look for an operative no-license, no-right-title-or-interest, ownership-retention, or equivalent clause concerning Confidential Information or rights embodied in it. Such a denial supports the hypothesis even if the Receiving Party has a limited contractual permission to use or disclose information; limited use is not a grant of ownership or intellectual-property rights. Conversely, ordinary access, possession, confidentiality, or purpose clauses neither support nor oppose the no-right statement. Cite all independently operative ownership and no-grant provisions needed to establish the denial.

Read the Confidential Information definition and incorporated list as a whole. Any covered non-technical category—such as business, financial, commercial, contractual, personnel, customer, or marketing information—opposes the assertion that only technical information is included. A general reference to information is not enough unless its stated categories or scope resolve the technical-only issue. Support would require an affirmative limitation of the entire definition to technical information. Cite the definition lead-in and the non-technical categories or exclusive limitation that determine the result.

Determine whether the agreement expressly keeps any substantive obligation effective after termination, expiration, or completion, or gives it a duration extending beyond that event. Support requires operative continuation language tied to obligations, not merely a return step, remedy, governing-law provision, employment consequence, or action that happens near termination. Cite the survival or duration clause and any referenced section needed to identify which obligation continues. If no obligation is carried past the endpoint, treat the hypothesis as unresolved.

Find an exclusion or permission specifically covering information independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of, access to, reference to, or reliance on Confidential Information. That provision supports the hypothesis subject to its proof conditions. Prior possession, public availability, third-party receipt, permitted use of the Disclosing Party's information, disclaimers, and authorization to conduct unrelated business do not establish independent development. Cite the exclusion lead-in, the independent-development limb, and any required no-use or documentary-proof condition.

Support the hypothesis only when the document permits or excludes from protection information received or obtained by the Receiving Party from an independent third party, ordinarily conditioned on that source having a lawful right to disclose and no confidentiality restriction. Do not substitute prior possession, independent development, the Disclosing Party's disclosure to others, generic third-party ownership, a no-warranty clause, or a prohibition on unauthorized acquisition. Cite the exceptions preamble, the third-party-receipt limb, and its source-right or no-duty conditions.

Identify the clause's disclosing actor and each expressly permitted recipient class. For the employee hypothesis, a need-to-know or confidentiality-conditioned permission to disclose to the Receiving Party's employees supports the statement. For the third-party hypothesis, support requires an affirmatively permitted external class such as agents, consultants, professional advisers, or representatives; employee-only permission does not transfer. A blanket prohibition, a consent mechanism for an unspecified third party, responsibility for recipients, or permission merely to use information does not itself authorize the relevant class. Cite the permission, recipient class, purpose or need condition, and binding-condition language; cite an operative class-specific prohibition when it opposes the statement.

Determine whether orally or verbally disclosed information can qualify as Confidential Information, including through a required later written confirmation or summary. Express oral coverage supports the hypothesis subject to any timing or identification condition. Do not infer oral coverage merely from broad words such as information, communications, discussions, meetings, observation, or individually identifiable information. Cite the definition or disclosure-form rule, the oral modality, and any follow-up writing condition. If the document neither includes nor excludes oral disclosures, treat the statement as unresolved.

Inspect whether the protected subject matter includes the existence, occurrence, status, terms, or contents of the agreement or the parties' negotiations, and whether the Receiving Party is barred from disclosing it. A prohibition supports the hypothesis; do not reverse polarity merely because the clause says the information shall not be disclosed. A clause protecting only underlying Confidential Information, or merely defining contracts generally, is insufficient unless its coverage and nondisclosure duty reach the agreement or negotiations at issue. Cite both the coverage provision and operative nondisclosure duty when they are separate.

Read the return-or-destruction rule together with every retention exception. An express right or necessity to keep an archival, compliance, backup, legally required, or infeasible-to-return copy after the return or destruction event supports the hypothesis within that exception. A requirement to return or destroy all information and copies, with no retention exception, opposes it. Ownership, possession before the event, permission to create copies, or permitted use during the agreement does not establish post-event retention. Cite the baseline disposition duty and the exception or no-retention language that resolves continued possession.

Separate permission to comply with compulsory process from a duty to notify the Disclosing Party. Support requires an operative requirement that the Receiving Party give notice, consultation, or equivalent warning when disclosure is required by law, regulation, court order, or legal process. A compelled-disclosure exception without that notice duty is unresolved, not support. Cite the compulsory trigger, notice actor and recipient, and any timing qualification such as prior, prompt, advance, or where possible; include cooperation language only when independently operative.

operations.rationale: No parent skill addresses nda-8. Cases 147 and 567 omitted genuine notice duties, while cases 285 and 214 treated a bare legal-disclosure exception as notice. The new record separates authorization to disclose from the distinct notice obligation.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Identify who is restrained, the protected person's relationship to the other party, and the prohibited recruiting conduct. Support requires an operative ban on the Receiving Party soliciting, inducing, recruiting, hiring, or interfering with at least some employees, representatives, or other personnel of the Disclosing Party, subject to stated duration, consent, advertisement, termination, or pre-existing-contact exceptions. A noncompetition clause, restriction on contacting persons for transaction information, or general nondisclosure duty does not establish non-solicitation. Cite the actor, protected class, prohibited action, duration, and operative exceptions.

operations.rationale: The parent has no nda-18 procedure and the current lawyer missed the operative non-solicitation provisions in cases 545 and 616. The new skill fixes the actor, recruiting action, protected personnel, and exceptions.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Determine whether the Receiving Party is operatively restricted to using Confidential Information only for a stated contractual purpose. Support requires a use limitation applying to the protected information, whether phrased as sole permitted use or a prohibition on every other use. A nondisclosure duty, access restriction, definition of the transaction, ownership clause, or statement that information was supplied for a purpose does not alone impose limited use. Cite each independently operative use restriction and the provision defining its referenced purpose; if the document regulates disclosure but not use, treat the hypothesis as unresolved.

operations.rationale: There is no nda-4 skill despite extensive evidence omissions and false support from nondisclosure language in case 390. The new record distinguishes an operative use restriction from purpose recitals, access controls, and disclosure duties.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Parse the disposition clause as actor, mandatory action, object, and trigger. Support only when the Receiving Party must return or destroy at least some Confidential Information because the agreement, relationship, services, transaction evaluation, or stated purpose terminates, expires, or ends. A duty activated solely by the Disclosing Party's request or demand does not establish this termination-triggered hypothesis, even if the agreement separately has a term or survival clause. Do not substitute ownership, certification, optional destruction, a right to request return, or a rule governing copies. Cite the operative trigger and duty together, plus any exception; if the trigger is only request-based or the obligated actor is different, treat the statement as unresolved.

operations.rationale: The existing trigger warning did not prevent seven request-only or wrong-actor clauses from being labeled as termination duties. This update requires the endpoint itself to activate the Receiving Party's disposition obligation and bars importing a separate term or survival provision.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Read the entire definition and test every route into Confidential Information. Support the universal only if every covered item must be marked, designated, identified, described as confidential, or subjected to the specified oral-confirmation procedure. A broad automatic category, coverage regardless of designation, or an alternative based on inherent nature or what a reasonable recipient should recognize opposes universality. A residual marking rule does not control earlier unmarked categories. When coverage requires information to be provided under circumstances that themselves indicate confidentiality, distinguish that affirmative disclosure condition from a reasonable-person inference based merely on nature or surrounding circumstances. Cite the definition lead-in, all operative identification routes, and every alternative that determines the universal; do not decide from one marking sentence alone.

operations.rationale: The current solver repeatedly omitted unmarked alternative routes, treated one marking limb as universal, and conflated disclosure under confidentiality-indicating circumstances with recipient inference from nature or circumstances. The update makes that source-grounded distinction explicit.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Support only when contractual text expressly carries at least one substantive obligation beyond termination, expiration, completion, or another identified endpoint. Identify both the continued obligation and the endpoint-relative continuation language. A fixed agreement term measured from execution or disclosure is insufficient unless the document connects it to an earlier termination or completion event. Return or destruction at an endpoint, assignment to successors, remedies for breach, governing law, employment consequences, and a clause merely remaining enforceable are not themselves surviving substantive obligations. Cite the survival or endpoint-relative duration clause and any referenced provision needed to identify what continues; otherwise treat the issue as unresolved.

operations.rationale: Eight neutral cases were still called survival based on return steps, remedies, successors, unrelated fixed terms, or general enforceability. The update now requires an identified substantive obligation and an express temporal link beyond an endpoint.

guidance.evidence_criterion: For each hypothesis separately, identify the Receiving Party as discloser and classify the expressly authorized recipient. Employee disclosure supports nda-5 only when employees of the Receiving Party are permitted recipients, subject to any need, purpose, notice, or confidentiality conditions. External agents, consultants, subcontractors, professional advisers, or representatives support nda-7 when affirmatively included; do not relabel them as employees merely because they act for the Receiving Party. Employee-only authorization combined with a ban on all other recipients opposes nda-7. A mechanism requiring case-specific consent for an otherwise unspecified third party, responsibility for a recipient, a third-party-acquisition exception, disclosure by the Disclosing Party, or permission merely to use information is not affirmative class permission. Cite the governing prohibition or permission, the exact class, and its operative conditions.

operations.rationale: Recipient-class errors persisted in both directions: agents and advisers were denied third-party status, employee-only clauses were extended externally, consent mechanisms were treated as class permission, and acquisition exceptions were mistaken for disclosure permission. The update makes actor direction and class identity decisive.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Track the direction of transfer. Support only when information comes to the Receiving Party from an independent source and the agreement excludes it from confidentiality or otherwise permits that acquisition, ordinarily because the source may lawfully disclose and owes no confidentiality duty. Do not use a clause about the Receiving Party disclosing information to outsiders, the Disclosing Party releasing information to others, third-party ownership, indemnification, recipient approval, prior possession, or independent development. Cite the exceptions lead-in, the receipt or acquisition limb, and every source-right, lawfulness, independence, or no-duty condition; without an incoming transfer to the Receiving Party, treat the hypothesis as unresolved.

operations.rationale: Five neutral cases were supported from outgoing disclosure, indemnity, or unrelated third-party references, and case 186 reversed a genuine incoming-source exclusion. The update narrows acquisition by transfer direction and replaces the overly broad generic third-party query.
